newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daito Kogyo seeks court protection - research firm.
newsitem.headline: Daito Kogyo seeks court protection - research firm.

text.p: Medium-sized Japanese construction company Daito Kogyo Co Ltd has applied for court protection from creditors under the nation's rehabilitation act, with debts of 154.4 billion yen, private research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said on Tuesday.
Daito Kogyo said it would hold a news conference regarding the application at 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Teikoku Databank said in a report that Daito, a Tokyo-based construction company capitalised at 6.19 billion yen, failed to receive financial support from creditor banks despite its difficulties.
Daito's debts totalled 154.4 billion yen at the end of March, including 25.1 billion yen in loan guarantees, the Teikoku report said.

Teikoku Databank also said in the report that Daito, whose shares were listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) in 1964, expanded into condominium and office building construction in the "bubble" era of inflated asset prices.
But its business deteriorated partly due to a slowdown in public works orders, along with less profitable private-sector construction contracts, it said.
In the 1996/97 business year that ended on March 31, the company posted a parent current profit of 1.57 billion yen on parent sales of 101.8 billion yen.
Shares in Daito Kogyo closed unchanged at 107 yen on Tuesday.
